The constraints that each hole’s boundary be disjoint from every other hole’s boundary and from the outer boundary force a minimum “protective” layer of polyomino cells around every hole. In the optimal construction the holes can be arranged with density \(1/3\) (one hole per \(3\times3\) block) while the surrounding polyomino cells occupy density \(2/3\) and remain edge‑connected. This yields an asymptotic ratio  

\[
\frac{h_n}{n} = \frac{\tfrac13}{\tfrac23}= \tfrac12 .
\]

The upper‑bound argument using vertex‑cover density and connectivity also shows that a higher ratio cannot be achieved. Therefore the limit is indeed \( \tfrac12\).
